rationale: In the thin hour before Europe opens (02:00-03:00 ET) the NQ book is as empty as in the Asian evening, so a price that pokes through a level where stops are known to rest and closes back inside has taken those stops with no real buyer or seller behind it and drifts back; the main setting is which resting-stop levels count. Losing side: The traders whose stops rest behind the prior-day, overnight, five-day and swing highs and lows, and the breakout chasers who buy the poke through them.
notes: liq: the highs and lows of the prior day, overnight, Asia, London, the evening before, the last 5 days and the last untraded swing (50 5-minute bars each side) and, on NQ, equal highs / lows are liquidity levels -> sweep = a bar trades beyond one and closes back inside: fade it; break = the first close beyond it: follow it; one signal per price per session
